{
  "IP": "neorv32_imem",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Instruction memory contents",
      "Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Information": "These are the instruction words held in the pre-initialized ROM or bus-written RAM, on which instruction fetches depend. They can enter as write data and leave as read data.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Confidentiality is at risk because memory contents reach rdata at lines 81, 95, 128-131 and 159-162 and are exposed through bus_rsp_o.data at line 185. Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data writes the RAM bytes at lines 116-125 and 145-154. Availability is at risk because rden can suppress bus_rsp_o.data at line 185 and the response acknowledge is reset or request-controlled at lines 172-180, allowing a memory transfer to be withheld.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "A hostile bus master could read instruction words through bus_rsp_o.data, overwrite RAM-backed instructions with bus_req_i.data, or hold reset or prevent valid read responses so instruction fetches are unavailable.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        116,
        119,

        125,
        145,

      ],

        162
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        185
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Instruction-memory access address",
      "Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Information": "This is the address selecting which instruction-memory word a read or write accesses. Correct fetches and writes depend on the selector choosing the intended word.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.addr is copied into addr at line 101, and addr selects the word read or written at lines 116-131 and 145-162, so altering it can redirect an access to a different instruction word.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"

      "Attack": "A hostile requester could alter bus_req_i.addr to redirect an instruction fetch or memory write to a different word.",
      "Enters Through": [

    {
      "Candidate Name": "Memory access command fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_imem",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The strobe, read/write direction and byte-enable fields only describe the access to the memory, so the Access command fields rule treats them as part of the access rather than information of their own (114-125, 143-154, 176-180)."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus response handshake status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_imem",

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Memory build configuration",

conceptual assets.information: These are the instruction words held in the pre-initialized ROM or bus-written RAM, on which instruction fetches depend. They can enter as write data and leave as read data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because memory contents reach rdata at lines 81, 95, 128-131 and 159-162 and are exposed through bus_rsp_o.data at line 185. Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data writes the RAM bytes at lines 116-125 and 145-154. Availability is at risk because rden can suppress bus_rsp_o.data at line 185 and the response acknowledge is reset or request-controlled at lines 172-180, allowing a memory transfer to be withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: A hostile bus master could read instruction words through bus_rsp_o.data, overwrite RAM-backed instructions with bus_req_i.data, or hold reset or prevent valid read responses so instruction fetches are unavailable.

conceptual assets.information: This is the address selecting which instruction-memory word a read or write accesses. Correct fetches and writes depend on the selector choosing the intended word.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.addr is copied into addr at line 101, and addr selects the word read or written at lines 116-131 and 145-162, so altering it can redirect an access to a different instruction word.
conceptual assets.attack: A hostile requester could alter bus_req_i.addr to redirect an instruction fetch or memory write to a different word.

considered, not kept.reason: The strobe, read/write direction and byte-enable fields only describe the access to the memory, so the Access command fields rule treats them as part of the access rather than information of their own (114-125, 143-154, 176-180).
The acknowledge is a re-timed request indication and the error field is tied to a constant, so the bus-handshake-copy rule bars a separate status asset (172-186).
The clock and reset only time or reset internal elements, and the Clocks and resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets (28-29, 170-180).
IMEM_SIZE and IMEM_INIT are generics that fix memory size and ROM/RAM selection at build time, so the Build-time values rule excludes them from runtime conceptual assets (23-25, 73-109).
